title: Outbreak Containment, CAPA & Crop Recovery
level: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist pathway
Cultivation personnel responsible for outbreak triage, containment, affected-scope reconstruction, corrective action, recovery monitoring and escalation
prerequisites: Plant Disease, HLVd & Biosecurity and Biological/Cultural Controls, Thresholds & Resistance Management or equivalent specialist foundation
evidencePolicy: Outbreak and CAPA instruction reuses controlled cannabis plant-health/IPM evidence plus quality-system/data-integrity sources. Containment is a risk-control action rather than proof of diagnosis; root cause requires evidence; CAPA closure requires effectiveness evidence; disposition/release remains role- and jurisdiction-controlled.
assessmentPolicy: The dedicated specialist assessment is development-only until exact-version technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize regulated product release, pesticide use, destruction, quarantine release or final laboratory interpretation.
description: Develops specialist response to pest, disease and plant-health outbreaks from first signal through containment, affected-scope reconstruction, causal analysis, CAPA, crop recovery verification, recurrence review and evidence-based handoff.
learningOutcomes: Triage an outbreak signal by separating immediate safety/spread controls from diagnostic certainty, preserving identity, affected scope and unresolved uncertainty.
Reconstruct outbreak distribution and likely pathways using time, location, plant/lot identity, movement history, environment, scouting and testing evidence.
Differentiate root cause, contributing factors, correlation and unsupported hypotheses and select corrective actions proportional to the evidence and consequence.
Design a CAPA and recovery plan with owners, due dates, containment, corrective/preventive actions, compatible recovery metrics and predefined effectiveness checks.
Determine whether an outbreak can be closed, escalated or reopened using comparable follow-up evidence, recurrence signals, disposition authority and reconstructable records.
